title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: Strategy is what management says on the earnings call; execution is what shows up in capacity utilization, debtor days, and non-anchor OEM wins six quarters later.
epigraph.author: Institutional governance checklist

web_blocks.html: To monitor SEDEMAC without quarterly noise, investors should track six leading operational KPIs. These are: (1) ISG & ISG+EFI penetration across domestic and export 2W/3W platforms; (2) EV MCU (ISAAC) attach rate; and (3) Industrial CPCB IV+ & export genset share. Investors must also watch (4) R&D spend as a % of sales (~6–7%) [13], (5) Working-capital discipline (Debtor, Inventory, and Payable Days) [1], and (6) Plant utilization across MF1, MF3, MF4, and MF5 [5].

web_blocks.takeaway: Operational health is currently PASS_WITH_WATCH: top-line and R&D KPIs are firing on all cylinders, but Debtor Days stretching to 46.1 days and heavy MF3/MF5 capex require strict execution discipline [1, 5].

web_blocks.html: Structurally, SEDEMAC's total addressable market (TAM) extends beyond domestic scooters. Management's H1 FY27 roadmap highlights four growth vectors. These include export three-wheeler ISG ECUs and ISG adoption on variant motorcycle models for top domestic OEMs [5]. They also include wet-magneto ISG kits for FY28 production, plus EV traction MCUs (ISAAC), electric machines (MF4), and CPCB IV+ industrial EFI controllers [5, 8, 9]. To support this pipeline, MF3 triples Chakan plant space and MF5 (Shoolagiri) adds South Indian OEM proximity [5].

web_blocks.title: CEO & Management Walk-the-Talk Audit (Prof. Shashikanth Suryanarayanan & Amit Dixit)
paragraphs: What Management Delivered: After commercializing sensorless ISG in 2018, leadership successfully scaled revenue 4.4x from ₹240 Cr (FY21) to ₹1,058 Cr (FY26), expanded OPM from 10–12% to 19–20%, captured ~75% of Indian genset AMF controllers, and brought MF3 into pilot production on schedule in Q2 FY27 [1, 5, 8]. On the November 3, 2026 concall, management candidly acknowledged H1 FY27 PCB/semiconductor cost headwinds (19.2% vs 21.4% YoY EBITDA margin) rather than masking them [5].

Where Skepticism Remains Warranted: Despite years of discussing OEM diversification, TVS Motor still represents ~75–81% of revenue [6, 13]. Meanwhile, management funded H1 FY27 capex and working-capital expansion (₹135 Cr to ₹258 Cr) by raising borrowings sharply from ₹72 Cr to ₹352 Cr [1, 5]. Investors should hold management to three measurable promises: (a) holding H2 FY27 EBITDA margins near H1 levels (~19%), (b) ramping MF3 to 65–70% utilization, and (c) converting growth back into positive Free Cash Flow once MF3/MF5 capex peaks [5].

book_paragraphs: Once you understand what a company makes and how its unit economics work, the next job is deciding which dashboard gauges actually matter. With SEDEMAC, watching quarterly net profit alone is like driving by looking only at the speedometer while ignoring the oil pressure. You need six leading operational KPIs on your screen.

First is ISG and ISG+EFI penetration alongside non-TVS OEM diversification. Today, ISG-related ECUs bring in roughly 60% to 64% or more of revenue, and TVS Motor writes roughly 75% to 81% of the checks. Management has won ISG and controller business with Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp, and is ramping export three-wheeler ISGs and wet-magneto kits targeted for FY28. The KPI to watch is simple: does TVS concentration steadily step down toward 60% and 50% over the next three years as those new programs scale?

Second is the commercial attach rate of EV Motor Control Units. Moving from 0.3% of mobility revenue in FY24 to meaningful production in FY26 and H1 FY27 is encouraging, and MF4's electric-machine shipments starting Q3 FY27 add another leg. Third is Industrial genset growth—₹146 crore in FY26, up 55%—driven by CPCB IV+ emission norms and North American OEMs. Fourth is R&D intensity, which has stayed around 6% to 7% of sales; in deep-tech controls, cutting R&D to flatter a single quarter's margin is eating your seed corn.

Fifth and sixth are the two gauges flashing amber right now: working-capital days and plant utilization. Debtor days stretched from 24 days in FY25 to 46.1 days in FY26, while inventory sits at 106 days and working capital jumped from ₹135 crore to ₹258 crore in H1 FY27. At the same time, MF1 is maxed out above 90% utilization, MF3's 120,000-square-foot Chakan plant just entered pilot production, and MF5 land has been acquired in Shoolagiri.

How does Founder and MD Prof. Shashikanth Suryanarayanan—alongside Joint MD Amit Dixit—score on a walk-the-talk audit? Give them genuine credit where it is due. They turned an IIT Bombay lab thesis into a ₹1,265 crore TTM run-rate electronics business, expanded operating margins from 10% in FY22 to 20% in FY26, and were refreshingly transparent on the November 3, 2026 earnings call about PCB inflation compressing H1 FY27 EBITDA margins from 21.4% to 19.2%. At the same time, keep your eyes wide open on two unfulfilled tests: diversifying away from TVS Motor has taken far longer than bulls hoped, and the sudden H1 FY27 jump in debt from ₹72 crore to ₹352 crore means MF3 must fill up toward its 65%–70% utilization target without stalling.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Management has earned high marks for engineering execution and candor on margin headwinds, but the next 18 months are a capital-allocation exam: ramping MF3 without letting debt-funded working capital erode returns on capital.

book_subsections.title: The TAM Runway: Domestic 2W/3W, Global Gensets, and EV Powertrains
paragraphs: When you step back from quarterly numbers and ask how large SEDEMAC can become over a five-to-ten-year horizon, the addressable runway breaks into three concentric rings. The inner ring is domestic two- and three-wheeler ICE micro-hybridization, where silent-start ISG and OBD Stage II-B EFI continue penetrating commuter motorcycles and export three-wheelers beyond scooters. The middle ring is electric two- and three-wheelers plus cordless power tools, where sensorless MCUs (ISAAC) and rare-earth-free motors (Logan) let SEDEMAC capture higher electronic content per vehicle as powertrains electrify. The outer ring is global industrial gensets, where CPCB IV+ compliance in India and gas/diesel EFI adoption in North America expand the dollar value of SEDEMAC's content per generator well beyond basic AMF panels.

What separates real TAM capture from slide-deck TAM is qualification velocity. Every new OEM platform takes 18 to 36 months of co-development before volume shipments begin. That is why tracking non-TVS design wins, MF3 utilization ramp toward 65%–70%, and EV MCU revenue share tells you far more about 2028 earnings power than any single quarter's top-line surprise.
